claims.text: Combining enhanced-sampling techniques with machine-learning interatomic potentials will enable thermodynamic integration between solid and liquid HEA phases.
The proposed method can determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and key liquid-phase properties.
The proposed method will achieve errors below 5%.
The target materials are equiatomic or near-equiatomic, complex multicomponent HEAs near their melting points.
The target HEA solids exhibit local lattice distortions.
Enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics using ML interatomic potentials can be used to perform thermodynamic integration across a solid-liquid interface.
The method is applicable across a broad range of equiatomic or near-equiatomic HEA compositions.
Transient solid-liquid interface structures and local chemical or ordering rearrangements occur during HEA melting.
Enhanced sampling efficiently explores the free-energy landscape and overcomes high-barrier transitions.
ML interatomic potentials provide rapid energy predictions.
ML interatomic potentials provide sufficiently accurate energy predictions for diverse HEA solid and liquid configurations.
The combination of enhanced sampling and ML potentials enables converged solid-liquid free-energy differences.
Converged free-energy differences directly yield melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change.
Computed melting and fusion properties will agree with high-throughput calorimetric benchmarks to within 5%.
The method will be efficient relative to existing approaches.
Rapid exploration of the large HEA compositional space requires efficient computational tools.
Traditional calorimetry, CALPHAD extrapolation, and ab initio molecular dynamics are computationally expensive or have limited throughput and accuracy across the entire HEA compositional space.
Performance for highly skewed HEA compositions or extreme conditions has not been validated.
ML-potential transferability across diverse HEA compositions and convergence for highly disordered liquids remain uncertain.
Deviation greater than 5% from independent experiments across multiple HEA compositions would falsify the proposed method.
